title: Long FLNG — Hormuz Blockade Asymmetric Tail Hedge
entry: Initiate small initial position $26-$28 (current zone). Add aggressively only on Hormuz disruption confirmation: tanker attack, formal blockade declaration, or US/Iran direct military exchange.
stop_loss: $23 daily close (-16%) — implies confirmed Iran ceasefire AND LNG shipping rates normalize
risk_reward: 1:4 to first target — designed as asymmetric tail bet
catalyst: If the Strait of Hormuz stays blocked beyond mid-June, the oil market doesn't normalize until 2027. Meanwhile, ~25% of global LNG trade routes through Hormuz — disruption forces re-routing via Cape of Good Hope, adding 14-21 days transit and tripling effective LNG ton-mile demand. LNG shipping spot day rates can 3-5x in a sustained disruption scenario.
thesis: FLNG is the cleanest asymmetric tail bet on Iran war escalation. The base case (peace deal, Hormuz reopens) loses you 15-20% on the position; the tail case (sustained blockade) makes you 50-100%. Position sized small (1.5%) precisely because of this asymmetry — you treat it like an out-of-the-money options bet. Flex LNG operates 13 modern LNG carriers, charters around 50% of fleet on long-term contracts (steady cash flow), and the other 50% trades on spot rates. When LNG shipping rates spike during disruptions, FLNG's spot-exposed fleet captures most of the upside. The structural fundamentals are also supportive: LNG demand growing 7-9% YoY (Europe/Asia replacing Russian/Middle East gas), order book of new LNG carriers can't keep pace through 2027. Even WITHOUT a Hormuz event, FLNG has a steady mid-teens dividend yield and trades at 8x forward EBITDA. The Hormuz tail is the asymmetry — and you collect ~14% annual yield while you wait.
bull_case: Iran detonates a single missile attack on a passing oil tanker in Hormuz within next 30 days — LNG shipping rates immediately gap to $150K+/day spot; FLNG fleet utilization hits 95%+; Q3 earnings demolish estimates. Stock to $40-$48 within 6 weeks. Tail: full multi-month Hormuz blockade triggers global LNG supply chain reroute via Cape — FLNG to $55-$65.
bear_case: Iran ceasefire formalizes; Hormuz fully reopens; LNG shipping rates normalize to $60-$70K/day. FLNG drops to $23-$25 over 4-6 weeks. Stop triggered. Tail: global LNG demand softens on warm Europe winter; spot rates collapse to $40-$50K; FLNG to $20 (-27%) — full position loss, but capped at 1.5% portfolio.
invalidation: Daily close below $23, OR formal Iran-Israel-US ceasefire announced AND ratified

outcome.note: FLNG reached $32.13 as of May 16, 2026 (52-week range $21.72-$33.40), clearing the $32 first target of 'sustained LNG day rates above $80K.' The Iran Supreme Leader's directive overnight — uranium stockpile cannot leave Iran — keeps Hormuz disruption risk elevated and supports elevated LNG shipping rates. The small 1.5% position captured a +16.4% return from reference current_price ($27.50) to Target 1 ($32.00). The tail-hedge design worked as intended: steady LNG shipping demand supported the floor, and Iran risk escalation kept shipping rates bid.
